entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6494"/><title type="x-s2">PSALM 86</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Ps.86.1-Ps.86.17">Psa 86:1-17</reference>. This is a prayer in which the writer, with deep emotion, mingles petitions and praises, now urgent for help, and now elated with hope, in view of former mercies. The occurrence of many terms and phrases peculiar to David's Psalms clearly intimates its authorship.</title> <div sID="gen9951" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6494"/><hi type="bold">1-2. poor and needy--</hi>a suffering child of God, as in <reference osisRef="Ps.10.12">Psa 10:12</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.10.17">17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.18.27">18:27</reference>.<div eID="gen9951" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen9952" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">I am holy--</hi>or, "godly," as in <reference osisRef="Ps.4.3">Psa 4:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.85.8">85:8</reference>. <div eID="gen9952" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: PSALM 86 Psa 86:1-17 . This is a prayer in which the writer, with deep emotion, mingles petitions and praises, now urgent for help, and now elated with hope, in view of former mercies. The occurrence of many terms and phrases peculiar to David's Psalms clearly intimates its authorship. 1-2. poor and needy-- a suffering child of God, as in Psa 10:12 , 17 ; 18:27 . I am holy-- or, "godly," as in Psa 4:3 ; 85:8 .
